newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 31.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Irish trainer Kevin Prendergast yesterday said that Gai Waterhouse's description of Melbourne Cup favourite Oscar Schindler as having "50 lengths" on the Australian and New Zealand horses was "a little ambitious". Page 22.

The Irish breeder-owner of Oscar Schindler paid the widow of Oscar Schindler A$199,000 for the right to name and race a colt he bred after the man who saved hundreds of Jews during the Second World War. Page 22.

The captain of the Socceroos, Paul Wade, yesterday announced his decision to quit after being the team's captain for six years. Wade said he was no longer up to the task of leading the Socceroos physically, but would play out his contract with the Canberra Cosmos. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

According to a leading Australian sports injury physician, the use of headgear would not have saved the life of Sydney rugby union player Ian Tucker when he collapsed and later died after making a tackle in a rugby game in Britain. Page 48.

The Bandette looks in strong form for the run of the Melbourne Cup after his run in the Werribee Cup yesterday. If he makes the field to run he could be an outside challenge to race favourite Oscar Schindler. Page 48.
Oscar Schindler looks to have an even better chance to win the Melbourne Cup after it was revealed that the course was to be watered at the request of the Oscar Schindler team.
THE AGE

Flemington racecourse manager Ross Bradfield is concerned that the Melbourne Cup course will be too dry this year, but his VRC colleagues are hoping for fine weather after rain has dogged the event for the past five years. Page B8.

Robert Allenby will miss next month's Australian Open in Sydney and the Greg Norman Classic and has abandoned his hope of playing golf again this year after complications with the injuries he sustained in a car accident in Spain a month ago. Page B8.

Yesterday's announcement that the Docklands site would house a new 52,000-seat stadium and that Waverley Park would be bulldozed, has led St Kilda to seek compensation as it has a 30-year contract to play games at Waverley Park. Page B8.
HERALD SUN

After failing to attend the first pre-season training run last Monday night, Gary Ablett turned up for practice last night. However, the Geelong superstar had a 90-minute meeting with coach Gary Ayres and is determined to attend the next six pre-Christmas training sessions. Page 96.

English trainer Ian Balding has further dampened the feeling in other Melbourne Cup horse camps with his comments yesterday that rival horse Oscar Schindler was up to six kilos under his deserved weight. Page 96.

Soccer Australia chief David Hill has resigned from his executive board position at the Oceania Football Confederation, saying that the organisation is retarding the development of the game in the region. The move follows the board's discussion of his supension after comments that may have already harmed the group. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

President of the Rugby Union Players' Association, Tony Dempsey, said yesterday that the new contracts offered to NSW rugby players had set industrial relations back 20 years, with some of the clauses in the new contracts particularly angering the Players Association. Page 88.

The Bathurst 1000 could be a victim in a war between rival television networks, as Channel Seven has the rights to telecast the event from Mt Panorama, but the new governing body of the race has a deal with Network Ten to have all the cars under contract or their new master. Page 86.

Following Shane Warne's career best figures of 5/35 in the one-day cricket match against Tasmania on the weekend, the Australian cricket team has been boosted by the hope that the leg spinner's form will continue to pick up after returning from a finger injury. Page 82.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
